claim: The spindle assembly checkpoint (SAC) temporally regulates mitosis by preventing progression from metaphase to anaphase until all chromosomes are correctly attached to the mitotic spindle.
source: The spindle assembly checkpoint (SAC) temporally regulates mitosis by preventing progression from metaphase to anaphase until all chromosomes are correctly attached to the mitotic spindle.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about SAC function, supported by the citations in the manuscript.

claim: Centrosomes refine the spatial organization of the mitotic spindle at the spindle poles.
source: Centrosomes refine the spatial organization of the mitotic spindle at the spindle poles.
evidence: This is established knowledge about centrosome function.

claim: Centrosome loss leads to elongated mitosis in mammalian cells.
source: However, centrosome loss leads to elongated mitosis, suggesting that centrosomes also inform the temporal organization of mitosis in mammalian cells.
evidence: This is supported by prior work and data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The mitotic delay in acentrosomal cells is enforced by the SAC in a MPS1-dependent manner.
source: Here, we find that the mitotic delay in acentrosomal cells is enforced by the SAC in a MPS1-dependent manner, and that a SAC-dependent mitotic delay is required for bipolar cell division to occur in acentrosomal cells.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data showing that MPS1 inhibition shortens mitosis in acentrosomal cells.

claim: A SAC-dependent mitotic delay is required for bipolar cell division to occur in acentrosomal cells.
source: Here, we find that the mitotic delay in acentrosomal cells is enforced by the SAC in a MPS1-dependent manner, and that a SAC-dependent mitotic delay is required for bipolar cell division to occur in acentrosomal cells.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by data showing division failure when MPS1 is inhibited in acentrosomal cells.

claim: Acentrosomal cells become polyploid.
source: Although acentrosomal cells become polyploid, polyploidy is not sufficient to cause dependency on a SAC-mediated delay to complete cell division.
evidence: This is supported by metaphase spread data showing increased chromosome numbers in acentrosomal cells.

claim: Polyploidy is not sufficient to cause dependency on a SAC-mediated delay to complete cell division.
source: Although acentrosomal cells become polyploid, polyploidy is not sufficient to cause dependency on a SAC-mediated delay to complete cell division.
evidence: This is supported by experiments showing that polyploid cells with centrosomes do not fail to divide when MPS1 is inhibited.

claim: The division failure in absence of MPS1 activity results from mitotic exit occurring before acentrosomal spindles can become bipolar.
source: Rather, the division failure in absence of MPS1 activity results from mitotic exit occurring before acentrosomal spindles can become bipolar.
evidence: This is supported by live imaging data showing monopolar spindles in acentrosomal cells treated with MPS1 inhibitor.

claim: Prevention of centrosome separation suffices to make cell division reliant on a SAC-dependent mitotic delay.
source: Furthermore, prevention of centrosome separation suffices to make cell division reliant on a SAC-dependent mitotic delay.
evidence: This is supported by experiments using STLC to prevent centrosome separation, which causes division failure when MPS1 is inhibited.

claim: Centrosomes and their definition of two spindle poles early in mitosis provide a 'timely two-ness' that allows cell division to occur in absence of a SAC-dependent mitotic delay.
source: Thus, centrosomes and their definition of two spindle poles early in mitosis provide a 'timely two-ness' that allows cell division to occur in absence of a SAC-dependent mitotic delay.
evidence: This is the main conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented.

claim: Depolymerization of microtubules and the resultant mitotic arrest before anaphase led to the discovery of the 'mitotic block'.
source: In eukaryotic cells, depolymerization of microtubules and the resultant mitotic arrest before anaphase led to the discovery of the 'mitotic block', (Levan, 1938; Rieder and Palazzo, 1992) now called the spindle assembly checkpoint (SAC).
evidence: This is historical information supported by citations.

claim: SAC activity prevents progression from metaphase to anaphase by inhibiting the anaphase-promoting complex/cyclosome (APC/C).
source: SAC activity prevents progression from metaphase to anaphase by inhibiting the anaphase-promoting complex/cyclosome (APC/C) (Fang, 2002; Muhua et al., 1998; Nilsson et al., 2008; Fang et al., 1998).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: The SAC is comprised of components largely enriched near kinetochores.
source: The SAC, comprised of components largely enriched near kinetochores, (Waters et al., 1998; Chen et al., 1996; Wang and Burke, 1995; Gurden et al., 2018) becomes activated when defects in chromosome attachment are present (Waters et al., 1998; Chen et al., 1996; O'Connell et al., 2008; Li and Benezra, 1996).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: The SAC becomes activated when defects in chromosome attachment are present.
source: The SAC, comprised of components largely enriched near kinetochores, (Waters et al., 1998; Chen et al., 1996; Wang and Burke, 1995; Gurden et al., 2018) becomes activated when defects in chromosome attachment are present (Waters et al., 1998; Chen et al., 1996; O'Connell et al., 2008; Li and Benezra, 1996).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Perturbance of spindle microtubules or certain microtubule motors leads to SAC activation.
source: Thus, perturbance of spindle microtubules or certain microtubule motors leads to SAC activation (Waters et al., 1998; Chen et al., 1996; Wang and Burke, 1995; Janssen et al., 2018; Kapoor et al., 2000).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Centrosomes are attached to and focus the spindle poles in a dynein-dependent manner.
source: At the other end of each side of the spindle apparatus, centrosomes are attached to and focus the spindle poles in a dynein-dependent manner (Heald et al., 1997; Walczak et al., 1998).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Centrosomes are usually comprised of two centrioles and pericentriolar material (PCM) that contains many microtubule nucleation factors that stabilize microtubule minus-ends.
source: Centrosomes are usually comprised of two centrioles and pericentriolar material (PCM) that contains many microtubule nucleation factors that stabilize microtubule minus-ends, and they are major loci of microtubule minus ends in the mitotic spindles of mammalian cells (Heald et al., 1997; Doxsey et al., 1994; Mitchison and Kirschner, 1984; Barr et al., 2010; Stearns and Kirschner, 1994).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Centrosomes are major loci of microtubule minus ends in the mitotic spindles of mammalian cells.
source: Centrosomes are usually comprised of two centrioles and pericentriolar material (PCM) that contains many microtubule nucleation factors that stabilize microtubule minus-ends, and they are major loci of microtubule minus ends in the mitotic spindles of mammalian cells (Heald et al., 1997; Doxsey et al., 1994; Mitchison and Kirschner, 1984; Barr et al., 2010; Stearns and Kirschner, 1994).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: In the absence of centrosomes, cultured mammalian cells can still divide bipolarly.
source: However, in the absence of centrosomes, cultured mammalian cells can still divide bipolarly (Khodjakov et al., 2000; Mahoney et al., 2006; Berns and Richardson, 1977).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Microtubules can be nucleated in mammalian cells by acentrosomal microtubule organizing centers (MTOCs).
source: Although centrosomes, when present, are major sites of microtubule nucleation, microtubules can be nucleated in mammalian cells by acentrosomal microtubule organizing centers (MTOCs; Watanabe et al., 2020; Chinen et al., 2021) as well as the chromatin-mediated microtubule nucleation pathway (Heald et al., 1996; Caudron et al., 2005; Petry et al., 2011).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Microtubules can be nucleated in mammalian cells by the chromatin-mediated microtubule nucleation pathway.
source: Although centrosomes, when present, are major sites of microtubule nucleation, microtubules can be nucleated in mammalian cells by acentrosomal microtubule organizing centers (MTOCs; Watanabe et al., 2020; Chinen et al., 2021) as well as the chromatin-mediated microtubule nucleation pathway (Heald et al., 1996; Caudron et al., 2005; Petry et al., 2011).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Absence of centrosomes alters bipolar spindle formation, such that spindles are monopolar early in mitosis and then resolve to become bipolar.
source: Nevertheless, absence of centrosomes alters bipolar spindle formation, such that spindles are monopolar early in mitosis and then resolve to become bipolar (Watanabe et al., 2020; Chinen et al., 2021; Chinen et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: The construction of acentrosomal spindles occurs during a mitosis that is, on average, elongated in time.
source: The construction of such acentrosomal spindles occurs during a mitosis that is, on average, elongated in time (Wong et al., 2015; Meitinger et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Acentriolar, hTERT-immortalized RPE-1 cells were generated through 10 d treatment with the PLK4 inhibitor centrinone (125 nM).
source: Acentriolar, hTERT-immortalized RPE-1 cells were generated though 10 d treatment with the PLK4 inhibitor centrinone (125 nM; Wong et al., 2015) or through deletion of SASS6 which encodes a structural protein (SASS6) that templates centriole duplication (Wang et al., 2015).
evidence: This describes the experimental method used, supported by citations.

claim: Acentriolar RPE-1 cells were generated through deletion of SASS6 which encodes a structural protein that templates centriole duplication.
source: Acentriolar, hTERT-immortalized RPE-1 cells were generated though 10 d treatment with the PLK4 inhibitor centrinone (125 nM; Wong et al., 2015) or through deletion of SASS6 which encodes a structural protein (SASS6) that templates centriole duplication (Wang et al., 2015).
evidence: This describes the experimental method used, supported by citations.

claim: Acentriolar RPE-1 cells were generated in TP53-/- background, since RPE-1 cells with an intact p53 pathway undergo G1 arrest in absence of centrioles.
source: Acentriolar RPE-1 cells were generated in TP53-/- background, since RPE-1 cells with an intact p53 pathway undergo G1 arrest in absence of centrioles (Wong et al., 2015; Meitinger et al., 2016).
evidence: This describes the experimental rationale, supported by citations.

claim: Acentriolar wild-type U2OS cells were generated through 10 d treatment with centrinone (125 nM).
source: Acentriolar wild-type U2OS cells, which are already p16-deficient (Koh et al., 1995) were generated through 10 d treatment with centrinone (125 nM).
evidence: This describes the experimental method used.

claim: U2OS cells are p16-deficient.
source: Acentriolar wild-type U2OS cells, which are already p16-deficient (Koh et al., 1995) were generated through 10 d treatment with centrinone (125 nM).
evidence: This is established knowledge about U2OS cells, supported by citation.

claim: RPE-1 TP53-/- and U2OS cells treated with centrinone showed significant increases in acentrosomal cells as compared to controls.
source: RPE-1 TP53-/- and U2OS cells treated with centrione showed significant increases in acentrosomal cells as compared to controls, as did TP53-/-; SASS6-/- cells in comparison to TP53-/-cells as measured by number of puncta positive for both γ-tubulin and centrin-3, which mark PCM and centrioles, respectively (Figure 1a and a').
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1a and quantified in 1a'.

claim: TP53-/-; SASS6-/- cells showed significant increases in acentrosomal cells in comparison to TP53-/- cells.
source: RPE-1 TP53-/- and U2OS cells treated with centrione showed significant increases in acentrosomal cells as compared to controls, as did TP53-/-; SASS6-/- cells in comparison to TP53-/-cells as measured by number of puncta positive for both γ-tubulin and centrin-3, which mark PCM and centrioles, respectively (Figure 1a and a').
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1a and quantified in 1a'.

claim: γ-tubulin and centrin-3 mark PCM and centrioles, respectively.
source: RPE-1 TP53-/- and U2OS cells treated with centrione showed significant increases in acentrosomal cells as compared to controls, as did TP53-/-; SASS6-/- cells in comparison to TP53-/-cells as measured by number of puncta positive for both γ-tubulin and centrin-3, which mark PCM and centrioles, respectively (Figure 1a and a').
evidence: This is established knowledge about these markers.

claim: The time required to complete mitosis was elongated in acentrosomal cells compared to controls.
source: As has been previously reported (Wong et al., 2015; Meitinger et al., 2016), the time required to complete mitosis was elongated in acentrosomal cells compared to controls (Figure 1b).
evidence: This is supported by live imaging data shown in Figure 1b and quantified in 1b', and is consistent with prior work.

claim: The time from nuclear envelope breakdown (NEBD) through anaphase onset was elongated in acentrosomal cells.
source: However, the mitoses were not uniformly elongated during each stage. Rather, the time from nuclear envelope breakdown (NEBD) through anaphase onset was elongated in acentrosomal cells, while the duration of anaphase through cytokinesis was not significantly different compared to controls (Figure 1b and b').
evidence: This is supported by live imaging data shown in Figure 1b and quantified in 1b'.

claim: The duration of anaphase through cytokinesis was not significantly different in acentrosomal cells compared to controls.
source: However, the mitoses were not uniformly elongated during each stage. Rather, the time from nuclear envelope breakdown (NEBD) through anaphase onset was elongated in acentrosomal cells, while the duration of anaphase through cytokinesis was not significantly different compared to controls (Figure 1b and b').
evidence: This is supported by live imaging data shown in Figure 1b and quantified in 1b'.

claim: The SAC is responsive to spindle defects that occur from NEBD through anaphase onset.
source: The SAC is responsive to spindle defects that occur from NEBD through anaphase onset, (Mansfeld et al., 2011) the elongated mitotic period in acentrosomal cells.
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: MPS1 (multipolar spindle 1) kinase is a necessary SAC component.
source: We inhibited MPS1 (multipolar spindle 1) kinase (also called Threonine Tyrosine Kinase, TTK), a necessary SAC component (Weiss and Winey, 1996; Abrieu et al., 2001) that begins high activity shortly before NEBD, (Kuijt et al., 2020) by treatment with CFI-402257 (Liu et al., 2016; Mason et al., 2017).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: MPS1 begins high activity shortly before NEBD.
source: We inhibited MPS1 (multipolar spindle 1) kinase (also called Threonine Tyrosine Kinase, TTK), a necessary SAC component (Weiss and Winey, 1996; Abrieu et al., 2001) that begins high activity shortly before NEBD, (Kuijt et al., 2020) by treatment with CFI-402257 (Liu et al., 2016; Mason et al., 2017).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: Both control and acentriolar cells treated with CFI-402257 showed reduced mitotic durations.
source: Both control and acentriolar cells treated with CFI-402257 showed reduced mitotic durations (Figure 1c and c') as measured by the time from visible NEBD to visible nuclear envelope reformation.
evidence: This is supported by live imaging data shown in Figure 1c and quantified in 1c'.

claim: MPS1 activity is necessary for the extended mitosis observed in acentrosomal cells.
source: Thus, MPS1 activity is necessary for the extended mitosis observed in acentrosomal cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the data showing that MPS1 inhibition shortens mitosis in acentrosomal cells.

claim: The majority of control cells treated with CFI-402257 underwent bipolar mitoses.
source: While the majority of control cells treated with CFI-402257 underwent bipolar mitoses, the majority of acentriolar cells treated with CFI-402257 rounded up and spread back out without dividing, producing a single daughter cell (Figure 1c and d).
evidence: This is supported by live imaging data shown in Figure 1c and quantified in 1d.

claim: The majority of acentriolar cells treated with CFI-402257 rounded up and spread back out without dividing, producing a single daughter cell.
source: While the majority of control cells treated with CFI-402257 underwent bipolar mitoses, the majority of acentriolar cells treated with CFI-402257 rounded up and spread back out without dividing, producing a single daughter cell (Figure 1c and d).
evidence: This is supported by live imaging data shown in Figure 1c and quantified in 1d.

claim: Acentriolar cells treated with MPS1-IN-1 underwent mitotic events that produced only one daughter cell.
source: Acentriolar cells treated with a different MPS1 inhibitor, MPS1-IN-1 (Kwiatkowski et al., 2010), also underwent mitotic events that produced only one daughter cell (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: The resultant cells from acentrosomal mitosis in CFI-402257 were mononucleate.
source: Examination of nuclear morphology revealed that the resultant cells were mononucleate, suggesting that they also failed to undergo nuclear division; however, the nuclei of acentrosomal cells after undergoing mitosis in CFI-402257 were highly abnormal in morphology (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by DAPI staining data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: The nuclei of acentrosomal cells after undergoing mitosis in CFI-402257 were highly abnormal in morphology.
source: Examination of nuclear morphology revealed that the resultant cells were mononucleate, suggesting that they also failed to undergo nuclear division; however, the nuclei of acentrosomal cells after undergoing mitosis in CFI-402257 were highly abnormal in morphology (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by DAPI staining data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: U2OS cells expressing N-terminally GFP-tagged α-tubulin (GFP-TUBA1B) from one allele of the TUBA1B locus were generated using CRISPR/Cas9-mediated homologous recombination.
source: To further examine mitosis in acentrosomal cells without MPS1 activity, we generated U2OS cells expressing N-terminally GFP-tagged α-tubulin (GFP-TUBA1B) from one allele of the TUBA1B locus, made using CRISPR/Cas9-mediated homologous recombination (Roberts et al., 2017; Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This describes the experimental method used, supported by citation and supplementary figure.

claim: In acentrosomal cells treated with centrinone and CFI-402257, a single α-tubulin punctum was present alongside condensed chromosomes during mitosis.
source: In the mitotic cell shown (Figure 1e), a single α-tubulin punctum was present alongside condensed chromosomes.
evidence: This is supported by live imaging data shown in Figure 1e.

claim: In acentrosomal cells treated with centrinone and CFI-402257, chromosomes eventually decondensed and a misshapen nucleus formed without cell division occurring.
source: While the chromosomes eventually decondensed, a misshapen nucleus formed without cell division occurring.
evidence: This is supported by live imaging data shown in Figure 1e.

claim: The phenotypes of elongated mitosis and sensitivity of cell division to MPS1 inhibition were reversible after 10 days of centrinone washout and return to normal centriole number.
source: The phenotypes observed, elongated mitosis and sensitivity of cell division to MPS1 inhibition, were reversible after 10 days of centrinone washout and return to normal centriole number (Figure 1—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 4.

claim: The cell division failure phenotype observed in acentriolar CFI-402257-treated cells could be prevented by treatment with proTAME.
source: The cell division failure phenotype observed in acentriolar CFI-402257-treated cells could be prevented by treatment with proTAME, (Zeng et al., 2010) an inhibitor of the APC/C (Figure 1f, Figure 1—figure supplement 1b).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1f.

claim: ProTAME is an inhibitor of the APC/C.
source: The cell division failure phenotype observed in acentriolar CFI-402257-treated cells could be prevented by treatment with proTAME, (Zeng et al., 2010) an inhibitor of the APC/C (Figure 1f, Figure 1—figure supplement 1b).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: ProTAME treatment resulted in a mitotic arrest of 6 hr or more, regardless of centrosome status.
source: ProTAME treatment resulted in a mitotic arrest of 6 hr or more, regardless of centrosome status, indicating that the rounding up/sitting down behavior of acentrosomal cells treated with MPS1 inhibitor truly represented mitotic entry and exit in the absence of cell division.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1f.

claim: Aurora B kinase is enriched at kinetochores and chromosomes during mitosis.
source: Aurora B kinase is enriched at kinetochores and chromosomes during mitosis and regulates a variety of SAC and error-correction components (Gurden et al., 2018; Santaguida et al., 2011; Roy et al., 2022; Liang et al., 2020).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Aurora B kinase regulates a variety of SAC and error-correction components.
source: Aurora B kinase is enriched at kinetochores and chromosomes during mitosis and regulates a variety of SAC and error-correction components (Gurden et al., 2018; Santaguida et al., 2011; Roy et al., 2022; Liang et al., 2020).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Both control and acentrosomal cells underwent elongated cell divisions when treated with AZD1152.
source: To perturb Aurora B function, we incubated cells with the Aurora B inhibitor AZD1152 (50 nM), also known as Barasertib, (Mortlock et al., 2007) and imaged cells live by phase microscopy (Figure 2a). Unlike with inhibition of MPS1, both control and acentrosomal cells underwent elongated cell divisions when treated with AZD1152 (Figure 2a').
evidence: This is supported by live imaging data shown in Figure 2a and quantified in 2a'.

claim: Both control and acentrosomal cells divided into two daughter cells the majority of the time when treated with AZD1152.
source: Furthermore, in contrast to treatment with MPS1 inhibitors, both control and acentrosomal cells divided into two daughter cells the majority of the time (Figure 2a'').
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 2a''.

claim: Co-treatment with MPS1 and Aurora B inhibitors resulted in shortened mitosis in the acentrosomal cells.
source: Co-treatment with MPS1 and Aurora B inhibitors resulted in shortened mitosis in the acentrosomal cells and resulted in a similar division failure rate as with MPS1 inhibition alone (Figure 2a–a'').
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 2a-a''.

claim: Co-treatment with MPS1 and Aurora B inhibitors resulted in a similar division failure rate as with MPS1 inhibition alone.
source: Co-treatment with MPS1 and Aurora B inhibitors resulted in shortened mitosis in the acentrosomal cells and resulted in a similar division failure rate as with MPS1 inhibition alone (Figure 2a–a'').
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 2a-a''.

claim: The mitotic delay caused by MPS1 activity is necessary for successful cell division in acentrosomal cells.
source: These results suggest that the mitotic delay caused by MPS1 activity is necessary for successful cell division in acentrosomal cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the Aurora B inhibition experiments.

claim: Treatment with both proTAME and CFI-402257 resulted in increased mitotic arrest (>6 hr) in cells regardless of MPS1 inhibition.
source: APC/C inhibition resulted in increased mitotic arrest (>6 hr) in cells regardless of MPS1 inhibition (Figure 1e).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1e (likely meant to be Figure 2b).

claim: Many of the acentrosomal cells treated with both proTAME and CFI-402257 eventually went on to divide, after the prolonged mitotic arrest.
source: However, many of the acentrosomal cells treated with both proTAME and CFI-402257 eventually went on to divide, after the prolonged mitotic arrest.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 2b-b''.

claim: Treatment with both proTAME and CFI-402257 resulted in majority bipolar divisions in acentrosomal cells.
source: Treatment with both proTAME and CFI-402257 resulted in majority bipolar divisions in acentrosomal cells (Figure 2b–b"), in contrast to treatment with CFI-402257 alone (Figure 1d).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 2b-b''.

claim: The division failure observed in acentrosomal cells treated with MPS1 inhibitor was due to mitotic shortening caused by preemptive anaphase onset and not other activities of MPS1.
source: This suggests that the division failure observed in acentrosomal cells treated with MPS1 inhibitor was due to mitotic shortening caused by preemptive anaphase onset and not other activities of MPS1.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the proTAME rescue experiments.

claim: Acentrosomal cell divisions are more prone to chromosome missegregation and fragmentation.
source: Acentrosomal cell divisions are more prone to chromosome missegregation and fragmentation, (Meitinger et al., 2016; Wang et al., 2020; Meitinger et al., 2020) and populations of acentrosomal cells cultured for multiple generations are more likely to be aneuploid (Wang et al., 2020).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Populations of acentrosomal cells cultured for multiple generations are more likely to be aneuploid.
source: Acentrosomal cell divisions are more prone to chromosome missegregation and fragmentation, (Meitinger et al., 2016; Wang et al., 2020; Meitinger et al., 2020) and populations of acentrosomal cells cultured for multiple generations are more likely to be aneuploid (Wang et al., 2020).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: Acentrosomal cells were polyploid as confirmed by counting chromosome pairs in metaphase spreads.
source: We confirmed that our acentrosomal cells were polyploid by counting chromosome pairs in metaphase spreads (Figure 3a).
evidence: This is supported by metaphase spread data shown in Figure 3a.

claim: SAC activity was required for the mitotic elongation in tetraploid acentrosomal mouse embryos.
source: In fact, previous results show that SAC activity was required for the mitotic elongation in tetraploid acentrosomal mouse embryos (Paim and FitzHarris, 2019) and that aneuploid cultured cells are more sensitive to SAC inhibition (Cohen-Sharir et al., 2021).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: Aneuploid cultured cells are more sensitive to SAC inhibition.
source: In fact, previous results show that SAC activity was required for the mitotic elongation in tetraploid acentrosomal mouse embryos (Paim and FitzHarris, 2019) and that aneuploid cultured cells are more sensitive to SAC inhibition (Cohen-Sharir et al., 2021).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: Treatment of RPE1 TP53-/- cells with 50 μM blebbistatin for 12 hr induced cytokinesis failure, resulting in a mixed population of binucleate cells and mononucleate cells.
source: We treated RPE1 TP53-/- cells with 50 μM blebbistatin, a myosin inhibitor (Straight et al., 2003), for 12 hr to induce cytokinesis failure, which resulted in a mixed population of binucleate cells resulting from division failure and mononucleate cells that had not entered mitosis during the incubation and served as an internal control for normal ploidy (Figure 3b).
evidence: This describes the experimental method used.

claim: Blebbistatin is a myosin inhibitor.
source: We treated RPE1 TP53-/- cells with 50 μM blebbistatin, a myosin inhibitor (Straight et al., 2003), for 12 hr to induce cytokinesis failure, which resulted in a mixed population of binucleate cells resulting from division failure and mononucleate cells that had not entered mitosis during the incubation and served as an internal control for normal ploidy (Figure 3b).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: Under treatment with CFI-402257, mononucleate RPE1 TP53-/- cells divided into two daughters the majority of the time.
source: Under treatment with CFI-402257, mononucleate RPE1 TP53-/- cells divided into two daughters the majority of the time (Figure 3c and c').
evidence: This is supported by live imaging data shown in Figure 3c and quantified in 3c'.

claim: Binucleate RPE1 TP53-/- cells divided the majority of the time under treatment with CFI-402257, into either two or multiple (3+) daughters.
source: Binucleate RPE1 TP53-/- cells divided the majority of the time, into either two or multiple (3+) daughters (Figure 3c and c').
evidence: This is supported by live imaging data shown in Figure 3c and quantified in 3c'.

claim: Polyploidy alone, as generated by cytokinesis failure, was not sufficient to cause division failure when MPS1 is inhibited.
source: Thus, polyploidy alone, as generated by cytokinesis failure, was not sufficient to cause division failure when MPS1 is inhibited.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the blebbistatin experiments.

claim: Control cells had two tubulin-dense MTOCs visible before NEBD.
source: While control cells had two tubulin-dense MTOCs visible before NEBD, acentrosomal cells only established two MTOCs well after NEBD and chromosome condensation (Figure 4a and a').
evidence: This is supported by live imaging data shown in Figure 4a and quantified in 4a'.

claim: Acentrosomal cells only established two MTOCs well after NEBD and chromosome condensation.
source: While control cells had two tubulin-dense MTOCs visible before NEBD, acentrosomal cells only established two MTOCs well after NEBD and chromosome condensation (Figure 4a and a').
evidence: This is supported by live imaging data shown in Figure 4a and quantified in 4a'.

claim: Treatment with STLC alone caused mitotic arrest.
source: As expected, treatment with STLC alone caused mitotic arrest (Figure 4b and b'); however, inhibiting MPS1 in addition to Eg5 resulted in exit from mitotic arrest and division failure (Figure 4b and b') similar to the phenotype observed in acentrosomal cells.
evidence: This is supported by live imaging data shown in Figure 4b and quantified in 4b'.

claim: Inhibiting MPS1 in addition to Eg5 resulted in exit from mitotic arrest and division failure similar to the phenotype observed in acentrosomal cells.
source: As expected, treatment with STLC alone caused mitotic arrest (Figure 4b and b'); however, inhibiting MPS1 in addition to Eg5 resulted in exit from mitotic arrest and division failure (Figure 4b and b') similar to the phenotype observed in acentrosomal cells.
evidence: This is supported by live imaging data shown in Figure 4b and quantified in 4b'.

claim: Cells treated with both Eg5 and MPS1 inhibitors formed monopolar spindles but then exited from mitosis, failing to divide.
source: Cells treated with both Eg5 and MPS1 inhibitors formed monopolar spindles but then exited from mitosis (Figure 4c), failing to divide.
evidence: This is supported by live imaging data shown in Figure 4c.

claim: Frequently some chromosomes became extruded during what appeared to be a highly asymmetric division in cells treated with both Eg5 and MPS1 inhibitors, with both centrosomes remaining unseparated in the primary cell.
source: However, frequently some chromosomes became extruded (Figure 4c, asterisk) during what appeared to be a highly asymmetric division, with both centrosomes remaining unseparated in the primary cell.
evidence: This is supported by live imaging data shown in Figure 4c.

claim: A midbody-like structure formed between the main resultant cell and the extruded portion in cells treated with both Eg5 and MPS1 inhibitors.
source: In addition, a midbody-like structure (Figure 4c, arrow) formed between the main resultant cell and the extruded portion.
evidence: This is supported by live imaging data shown in Figure 4c.

claim: The early separation of centrosomes prevents monopolar spindles from persisting, allowing a timely completion of mitosis without a requirement for SAC-mediated delay.
source: Taken together, these results show that the early separation of centrosomes prevents monopolar spindles from persisting, allowing a timely completion of mitosis without a requirement for SAC-mediated delay.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the STLC experiments.

claim: Acentrosomal cells rely on SAC-mediated delay to build a bipolar spindle and successfully divide into two daughters.
source: Here, we show that acentrosomal cells rely on SAC-mediated delay, not simply to correct chromosome attachment errors, but to build a bipolar spindle and successfully divide into two daughters (Figure 4d).
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the study, supported by all the experimental data.

claim: Centrosomes form two MTOCs very early in mitosis and can be efficiently separated into two spindle poles by Eg5 activity.
source: Because centrosomes form two MTOCs very early in mitosis and can be efficiently separated into two spindle poles by Eg5 activity, they provide a 'timely two-ness' to mitotic organization.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data and established knowledge.

claim: Rapid establishment of bipolarity normally allows cells to successfully divide in the absence of a SAC-induced delay.
source: This rapid establishment of bipolarity normally allows cells to successfully divide in the absence of a SAC-induced delay.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data.

claim: It is unclear why acentrosomal cells are prone to chromosome missegregation despite the ability to assemble bipolar spindles.
source: For instance, it it is unclear why acentrosomal cells, whether created in culture or during female meiosis in many metazoans, are prone to chromosome missegregation despite the ability to assemble bipolar spindles (Meitinger et al., 2016; Wang et al., 2020; Meitinger et al., 2020; Holubcová et al., 2015; Yoshida et al., 2020).
evidence: This is a statement about an open question in the field, supported by citations.

claim: SAC activity weakens over time during prolonged arrest, characterized by decreasing levels of cyclin B globally and MAD2 at kinetochores, thus enabling mitotic slippage.
source: It is known that SAC activity weakens over time during prolonged arrest, characterized by decreasing levels of cyclin B globally and MAD2 at kinetochores, thus enabling mitotic slippage (Lok et al., 2020; Brito and Rieder, 2006; Brito et al., 2008).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Centrosome presence or loss may be a relevant clinical marker to consider when predicting effects of MPS1 inhibition on division outcome.
source: Given our results, centrosome presence or loss may be a relevant clinical marker to consider when predicting effects of MPS1 inhibition on division outcome.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the findings of the study.

claim: STLC is an inhibitor of the bipolar kinesin Eg5 (also known as Kif11 or kinesin-5), resulting in monopolar mitotic spindles.
source: We treated RPE1 or U2OS cells containing centrosomes with (+)-S-Trityl-L-cysteine (STLC), an inhibitor of the bipolar kinesin Eg5 (also known as Kif11 or kinesin-5), resulting in monopolar mitotic spindles (Skoufias et al., 2006; Ogo et al., 2007).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Having two separate and functional MTOCs at the beginning of mitosis facilitates timely division, without requiring a SAC-mediated delay.
source: One possible explanation for the robustness of cell division in cells with centrosomes is that having two separate and functional MTOCs at the beginning of mitosis facilitates timely division, without requiring a SAC-mediated delay.
evidence: This is a hypothesis proposed based on the experimental observations.

claim: A monopolar spindle, such as in acentrosomal cells early in mitosis, is sufficient to cause division failure upon MPS1 inhibition, even in the presence of centrosomes.
source: We therefore tested whether a monopolar spindle, such as in acentrosomal cells early in mitosis, is sufficient to cause division failure upon MPS1 inhibition, even in the presence of centrosomes.
evidence: This is a hypothesis tested by the STLC experiments.
